title: The environment
hook: plant a tree, and whatever eats from it counts as charity for you
tomorrow: what did a thirsty dog teach a man at a well?

segments.voice: A week of service: feed people. Stop the oppressor. A word of truth. Two fingers together. Like the path of Allah. And yesterday, we were migrants. One more today, and it grows.
screen: `SIX LINES OF SERVICE.` → `WE WERE MIGRANTS.` → `ONE MORE, AND IT GROWS.`

segments.voice: Saturday, seven in the morning, a sign-up sheet for a tree planting. The saplings are knee-high. The shade they'll make is years away, long after the volunteers have moved on. So why bother? The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ answered with a strange kind of accounting. Don't count the shade. Count the bites.

In Sahih al-Bukhari: no Muslim plants a tree or sows a crop, and a bird, a person or an animal eats from it, but it counts as sadaqah, charity, for him. Every bite. The sparrow pecking a fig. The squirrel you'll never meet. One version in Sahih Muslim even adds: what's stolen from it counts too. So the tree is worth planting even if you never sit under it. The reward was never the shade. It's what the tree gives away. A saying in al-Adab al-Mufrad pushes it to the edge: if the Hour comes and one of you has a sapling in his hand, let him plant it. The Qur'an puts people in charge of the earth, not as owners. In Pickthall's words: "He it is Who hath placed you as viceroys of the earth." A viceroy looks after what belongs to someone else. Now look back at the week. It has the tree's shape: a plate, a stopped hand, a true word, a steady hour, a Sunday call, an open door. Each one feeds someone you may never see again.
screen: `A BIRD, A PERSON, AN ANIMAL.` · `EVEN WHAT'S STOLEN COUNTS.` · `PLANT IT, EVEN AT THE HOUR.` · `VICEROYS, NOT OWNERS.` · then, large: `EVERY BITE IS CHARITY.`

segments.voice: Count, slowly, the living things that fed you today without knowing it: the wheat in the bread, the tree behind the paper, the bee somewhere behind the honey. Give each one a breath, as many as come.
The environment: the living world in our care. In the hadith, whatever eats from what you plant counts as charity.
Something to keep: every bite is charity, even the ones you never see. That's the week, planted.

screen: `DAY 1743 COUNTS.` → `SERVICE AND JUSTICE · 8 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DID A THIRSTY DOG TEACH A MAN?`

howItsDone: Muslims plant trees, keep gardens and give fruit away with this hadith in mind, and some mosques and Muslim groups organize tree plantings and clean-ups as acts of sadaqah.

al-Adab al-Mufrad.meaning: a book of hadith on manners, gathered by al-Bukhari

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds

viceroys.meaning: people who govern on someone else's behalf; stewards

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2320 (also Sahih Muslim 1553): no Muslim plants a tree or sows a crop and a bird, a person or an animal eats from it, but it is charity for him
